subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Wrigley and Kielland Forceps, Ventouse, Symphysiotomy and Robson

steps.tx: Short lightweight forceps for outlet and lift out deliveries are **Wrigley forceps**. Their small pelvic curve suits the perineal head and caesarean extraction. They cannot rotate or deliver a head still in the mid cavity. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Wrigley forceps are short outlet forceps that cannot rotate mid cavity heads.

steps.tx: The sliding lock forceps designed to rotate the head in the midpelvis are **Kielland forceps**. In expert hands they convert deep transverse arrest to vaginal delivery. Their use has declined with caesarean safety, concentrating expertise dangerously. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Kielland forceps rotate midpelvic heads in expert hands, now increasingly rare.

steps.tx: Vacuum extraction with a cup on the fetal scalp is the **ventouse**. Metal and silicone cups suit different situations, and the chignon swelling it raises resolves in days. It needs maternal effort, fails more than forceps, but injures mothers less. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Ventouse vacuum extraction injures mothers less but fails more than forceps.

steps.tx: The artificial caput raised under the vacuum cup during extraction is the **chignon**. It looks alarming and crosses the scalp freely, settling within forty eight hours. Parents are warned before delivery to prevent distress at first sight. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: The chignon under the vacuum cup settles within forty eight hours.

steps.tx: Operations destroying and extracting a dead fetus to save the mother, now rare, are **destructive operations**. Craniotomy for hydrocephalus or dead obstructed fetus persists where caesarean is impossible or lethal. Their decline mirrors caesarean access. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Destructive operations for dead obstructed fetuses persist only where caesarean is impossible.

steps.tx: Dividing the pubic symphysis cartilage to enlarge the pelvis is **symphysiotomy**. It permanently widens the outlet for future births, unlike caesarean scars. Where transport or theatre is absent it still saves mothers from obstructed labour. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Symphysiotomy permanently widens the pelvis where caesarean access is absent.

steps.tx: The ten group classification auditing every caesarean by obstetric category is the **Robson classification**. Nulliparous term cephalic spontaneous labour is group one, previous caesarean group five. Comparing like groups reveals true practice variation between units. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Robson classification audits caesareans in ten comparable obstetric groups.

steps.tx: Prerequisites for instrumental delivery include full dilation, engagement, known position and analgesia, summarised as **instrumental criteria**. A senior must be able to abandon and proceed to caesarean at any point. Trial in theatre suits borderline cases. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Instrumental criteria demand full dilation, engagement, known position and caesarean backup.

steps.tx: Sequential instrument use, vacuum then forceps, multiplies neonatal injury and is discouraged as **sequential instrumentation**. One failed instrument means caesarean in most modern protocols. The exception is an expert completing an almost delivered head. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Sequential instrumentation multiplies injury, so one failed instrument means caesarean.
